title: Encryption change traceback playground & evidence conciliator
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: build a lightweight sandbox (traceback playground) and a reconciler service (evidence conciliator) to produce tamper-evident, queryable bundles tying key lifecycle events to residency and retention artifacts. This task targets automation of encryption evidence for audit requests and to reduce manual evidence assembly during compliance reviews.

Motivation and scope:
- Current postmortem and audit workflows require manual correlation between KMS/HSM rotation events, tenant residency metadata, and retention purge logs. That process is error-prone and costly during SOC/PCI/REDA audits.
- We will provide a reproducible playground for simulating key rotations, ephemeral wraps, and cross-region key mirror events so reviewers can trace the exact sequence that produced an encrypted object.
- The reconciler service will consume rotation streams and storage retention logs to emit signed evidence bundles (JSONL with signatures) that map key material IDs, wrapped keys, rotation timeline, KMS key versions, and counterparty residency stamps.

Non-goals: full enterprise attestation portal and legal-ready PDFs — those will be downstream consumers of the evidence bundles. This ticket focuses on core producer: playground + conciliator + evidence schema.

Technical summary and decisions so far:
- Ingests: KMS event stream (CloudKMS / AWS CloudTrail / HSM syslog), object storage retention events (bucket lifecycle notifications), and internal tenancy-residency table.
- Evidence format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) with canonical keys, SHA-256 content digests, and an envelope signature using a signing key in HSM. We will version the schema v1.0.
- Replayability: the playground supports deterministic replay of synthetic rotation + retention events (seeded RNG) to validate reconciler behavior in CI.
- Placement: conciliator will be a small service in infra namespace with read-only access to event streams and a write sink to the evidence S3 (or equivalent) bucket. Signed-bundles are ACL-restricted and lifecycle-managed per retention policy.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Playground can reproduce at least 3 rotation scenarios (single region rotation, cross-region mirror rotation, and emergency rollback) and produce a canonical event trace.
- Conciliator produces signed evidence bundles for >99% of ingested rotation+retention pairs in a staging run.
- Evidence bundle schema documented in Confluence and stable (v1.0).
- End-to-end test in CI that replays a synthetic incident and validates that the bundle contains the expected rotation timestamps, key IDs, and residency tags.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: exposing internal key metadata. Mitigation: conciliator runs with least privilege, bundles contain only key identifiers (no raw material) and are encrypted with tenant-scoped envelopes.
- Risk: signature key compromise. Mitigation: signature key lives in customer-managed HSM or Redwood HSM with strict rotation and audit.

Next milestones:
- 2025-02-18: initial PoC playground + schema draft (done, see PR).
- 2025-02-22: conciliator skeleton that consumes CloudTrail and writes signed JSONL bundles to evidence bucket (in progress).
- 2025-03-04: CI replay tests and Confluence runbook for auditors.

Links to artifacts and onboarding docs are below in dedicated fields.

Notes: this work will enable downstream UI/console features for fast evidence retrieval and will integrate with the existing residency attestation pipelines once schema is stable. Reviewers: PM and Security must sign off on schema and threat model before enabling production write privileges.
acceptance_criteria: Playground reproduces single-region rotation, cross-region mirror, and emergency rollback scenarios
Conciliator emits v1.0 signed JSONL bundles for >=99% of matched event pairs in staging
Evidence schema documented and approved on Confluence
CI replay validates mapping between rotation events, key versions, and residency tags
approach: 1) Implement deterministic event generator (playground) with configurable seeds and scenario YAMLs. 2) Build conciliator service that subscribes to event streams, correlates by object-id + tenant-id + time-window, and produces canonical JSONL bundles. 3) Sign bundles using HSM-backed signing key and push to restricted evidence bucket. 4) Add CI replay and unit tests against schema validators. 5) Run security review and add hardening (rate limits, query quotas, audit logs).
